name: Fred E Cohen
current_role: Co-founder & Chairman, Monograph Capital; Co-founder & Senior Managing Director, Vida Ventures; director at Intellia, CareDx, Kyverna
profile: Physician-scientist (Yale BS, Oxford DPhil as a Rhodes Scholar, Stanford MD) who spent 1980-2014 at UCSF, including as Chief of Endocrinology and Metabolism. Co-founded TPG Biotech (2001-2016), then Vida Ventures (2017) and Monograph Capital; sits on several biotech boards.
interesting_fact: Has published 200+ peer-reviewed papers, is co-inventor on 10+ patents, and was elected to the National Academy of Medicine (2004) and American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2008).
deep_cut_fact: His UCSF research covered prion diseases and structure-based drug design, and he shared the LVMH 'Science pour l'art' prize with Nobel laureate Stanley Prusiner.
notes: Best route is via Monograph Capital's published media/info emails. Biotech investor; little energy/data-center overlap beyond computational biology.

name: David Livingstone
current_role: Chief Client Officer, Citigroup (since Sept 2023); member of Citi's Executive Management Team
profile: Australian-born investment banker who spent 16+ years in M&A at Goldman Sachs, then HSBC and Credit Suisse (CEO of Credit Suisse Australia 2010-13). Joined Citi in 2016 as Country Officer for Australia/NZ, ran Citi EMEA for nearly five years, and since 2023 leads Citi's global client coverage as Chief Client Officer.
interesting_fact: As Citi's EMEA CEO he steered the bank through Brexit and the pandemic in its largest region, and led Citi's global response to the war in Ukraine and resulting Russia sanctions.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking leadership he studied economics (BA Hons) at Macquarie University in Sydney and then took a law degree at Jesus College, Cambridge; he spent over 16 years in Goldman Sachs' M&A department.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; route via Citi media relations (press-release media contact). Common name - many unrelated David Livingstones online.

name: Josh Hirsberg
current_role: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer, Boyd Gaming Corporation (CFO since Jan 2008)
profile: Long-serving gaming-industry finance executive; Boyd Gaming CFO since 2008 (EVP since 2016), overseeing accounting, budgeting, capital allocation and investor relations. Previously held finance and investor-relations roles at Harrah's/Caesars Entertainment and was CFO of a Las Vegas resort developer. Still fronting Boyd's earnings calls in 2026.
interesting_fact: Has been Boyd's CFO for nearly 19 years, through the 2008 financial crisis and the pandemic; by 2026 he was reporting leverage of under 2x on roughly $1B in quarterly revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Immediately before Boyd he was CFO of Edge-Star Partners, a Las Vegas resort development company (2006-07), after serving as Vice President, Treasurer and Investor Relations at Caesars Entertainment from 2002.
notes: Boyd's press releases list Hirsberg himself as the 'Financial Contact' with his work email (Q3 2026 release); David Strow is the media contact.

name: M Jay Allison
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Comstock Resources Inc. (Frisco, Texas)
profile: Former Midland oil-and-gas attorney who co-founded a private E&P in 1983 that took over Comstock Resources in 1987; CEO since 1988 and chairman since 1997. Since Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones became the controlling shareholder in 2018-19, Allison has refocused Comstock on Haynesville natural gas, including the Western Haynesville play aimed at Gulf Coast LNG and power demand.
interesting_fact: Jerry Jones says Allison pitched him an investment about 30 years before their 2018 deal and he passed; Jones later put in roughly $1.1B and ended up owning about 75% of Comstock.
deep_cut_fact: Played Baylor football under coach Grant Teaff and recalls his freshman-year team erasing a 24-point halftime deficit to beat Texas, en route to the 1975 Cotton Bowl; he went on to earn three Baylor degrees (BBA, MS, JD) and served on Baylor's Board of Regents.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (Haynesville gas, LNG and power demand). Best route is Comstock investor relations (Ron Mills). Outspoken Christian; values-driven quotes in Baylor profile. Comstock's Q3 2026 release lists Ron Mills, VP of Finance and Investor Relations, (972) 668-8834 as company contact (no email published).

name: Ryan D. Taylor
current_role: Chief Revenue Officer and Chief Legal Officer, Palantir Technologies
profile: Stanford-trained computer scientist and Harvard Law graduate who left Covington & Burling to join Palantir in 2010. Became Chief Legal and Business Affairs Officer around the 2020 listing and since 2023 has held an unusual dual role running both Palantir's revenue organisation and its legal function.
interesting_fact: Holds the rare combination of Chief Revenue Officer and Chief Legal Officer at a large public tech company; his 2025 pay package was reported at about $28M.
deep_cut_fact: Before law school he earned both a B.S. in Computer Science and an M.S. in Management Science & Engineering at Stanford, so Palantir's top lawyer is also a trained engineer.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts verified. Route via Palantir media relations. Relevant to AI/data-center angle via Palantir's AIP commercial growth.

name: Jeffrey Likosar
current_role: President, Corporate Development & Transformation and Chief Financial Officer, ADT Inc.
profile: Finance executive who joined ADT in 2016 ahead of its 2018 IPO and has been CFO in two stints (2017-2022 and again since 2024, interim from Dec 2023), also running corporate development, strategy and transformation. Previously CFO of Gardner Denver and held finance roles at Dell and GE.
interesting_fact: ADT brought him back as CFO in 2024 after a 'robust search' while letting him keep his strategy and transformation remit, making him one of the few CFOs who also formally runs corporate development and transformation.
deep_cut_fact: Started his career in GE's finance ranks, holding executive finance roles across GE's Appliances, Plastics and Aviation divisions, before Dell and Gardner Denver; he is a UNC Kenan-Flagler business graduate.
notes: Corporate executive with low public profile; route via ADT media relations or IR.

name: Tod E. Carpenter
current_role: Executive Chairman, Donaldson Company (CEO 2015-March 2026); independent director, AMETEK
profile: Engineer-turned-executive who spent 13 years at Hughes Aircraft, joined Minneapolis filtration maker Donaldson in 1996 (gas turbine systems), and rose to President & CEO (2015) and Chairman (2017). Handed the CEO role to COO Richard Lewis on March 2, 2026 and became Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: Donaldson's filters range from fingernail-sized units protecting computer disk drives to house-sized systems for gas turbines that keep power grids running - a direct link to energy and data-center infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: He first met Donaldson as an outside IT/management consultant in the Twin Cities (1994), working with its Gas Turbine Systems group, after he and his wife decided to move back to the Midwest and build careers around that choice; he joined in 1996 as director of GTS operations.
notes: Recently transitioned from CEO to Executive Chairman (2026) - may have more time for interviews. Member of the Carlson School (U of Minnesota) Board of Advisors. Press-release contact is Sarika Dhadwal (IR/communications).

name: Ankur Sinha
current_role: Chief Product and Technology Officer, Remitly Global (since Nov 2024; CTO Feb 2022-Nov 2024)
profile: Indian-born technologist who co-founded an Indian startup, spent 12 years at Microsoft (rising to Senior Director for multiple services & experiences) and ran commerce technologies in Google Cloud as an Engineering Director. Joined Seattle remittance fintech Remitly as CTO in 2022 and now leads both product and engineering.
interesting_fact: Oversees the product and engineering behind Remitly, a cross-border money-transfer platform for immigrants sending money home, after leading commerce technology for Google Cloud.
deep_cut_fact: Co-founded and was CTO of RA Systems, a technology startup in India, from June 2001 to December 2006 - founded when he was still a teenager (he was 42 in April 2026) - before joining Microsoft in 2007.
notes: Corporate executive; speaks at fintech conferences (Finovate etc.). Route via Remitly press office.

name: Marcin Zukowski
current_role: Snowflake co-founder; left Snowflake in 2024, now an investor and consultant (per CWI, Nov 2024)
profile: Polish computer scientist whose CWI Amsterdam PhD pioneered vectorized query execution; co-founded CWI spin-off VectorWise (acquired by Actian) and in 2012 became Snowflake's third co-founder with Benoit Dageville and Thierry Cruanes, building and leading its early engineering team. Left Snowflake in 2024; now invests, consults and supports tech innovation in Poland.
interesting_fact: His 2009 PhD thesis laid out the blueprint for two core Snowflake technologies - vectorized execution and lightweight columnar compression - and the VectorWise paper won the CIDR 2024 Test of Time Award.
deep_cut_fact: In November 2024 CWI awarded him its Dijkstra Fellowship; he has said the vectorized-execution idea behind X100 came only because he worked on MonetDB - and he originally came to Amsterdam wanting to do a more theoretical databases MSc thesis at Vrije Universiteit.
notes: No verified published contact found in the time available (web-search budget exhausted). Possible route via CWI Amsterdam connections. Very relevant to data-infrastructure topics.

name: Joshua Reeves
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Gusto (San Francisco)
profile: Stanford electrical-engineering graduate and repeat founder who co-founded ZenPayroll in 2011 with Edward Kim and Tomer London (Y Combinator W12); renamed Gusto in 2015, it grew into a payroll, benefits and HR platform for small businesses. Gusto was valued around $9.3-9.6B and reportedly passed $1B in annual revenue by early 2026.
interesting_fact: Gusto began as ZenPayroll after co-founder Eddie Kim watched his mother do the payroll for the family medical practice by hand for two decades, at a cost of as much as $200,000 in tax penalties over the years.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Tomer London by chance through Stanford's alumni mentorship program, which paired Reeves with London a few months into London's EE PhD; Reeves and Kim had reconnected after Kim ran a half-marathon with zero training to win a bet.
notes: Still private (no SEC filings); no press email verified (gusto.com blocked automated fetches; web-search budget exhausted). X/LinkedIn handles are as listed on his Y Combinator founder profile.

name: Sandeep Aggarwal
current_role: Founder & CEO, Droom (Indian online automobile marketplace), per Droom's website
profile: Former top-ranked Silicon Valley internet equity analyst (Citigroup, Oppenheimer, Collins Stewart) who founded ShopClues from his California home in 2010, then launched Droom in 2014 as an online marketplace for new and used vehicles in India. Bills himself as the only Indian tech founder to build two unicorns back-to-back; Droom has talked of an IPO.
interesting_fact: ShopClues became India's 5th consumer-internet unicorn despite being, by his count, the 35th entrant into Indian e-commerce; he later served as a judge ('master') on MTV Dropout, an Indian reality show about entrepreneurship.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he worked in strategy-planning roles at Microsoft in Redmond and at Schwab.com in San Francisco; he holds a US patent and an MBA from Washington University in St. Louis.
notes: Very media-friendly: runs a personal site with a 'Invite as Speaker' form and media kit, YouTube channel and podcast section - best route for a podcast invite. Droom's current valuation/IPO status not re-verified for 2026.

name: Adrian Durham
current_role: Non-Executive Founding Director (board member and major shareholder), FNZ Group
profile: Founder of FNZ, the global wealth-management platform, which he started in 2003 and led as Group CEO for about two decades as it expanded from New Zealand to the UK (2005) and worldwide. Stepped down as CEO in September 2024 (succeeded by Blythe Masters) and remains on the board as non-executive founding director, senior adviser and major shareholder.
interesting_fact: FNZ, which he built into a multi-billion-dollar wealth-tech platform backed by investors such as Temasek, La Caisse and Generation Investment Management, began life in 2003 as a business unit inside the New Zealand branch of Credit Suisse.
deep_cut_fact: FNZ's name comes from First NZ Capital; it was spun free in a January 2009 management buyout backed by H.I.G. Capital valued at just NZ$34 million.
notes: Very private; few interviews. FNZ leadership page (Nov 2026) lists Stephen Welch as Executive Group Chair and Interim Group CEO. Best route via FNZ corporate contact/media toolkit page.

name: Brien Colwell
current_role: Appears to be working on URnetwork (UR Foundation / BringYour, Inc.), a decentralized privacy network - per his LinkedIn; not independently confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun as co-founder of HeadSpin, the Palo Alto mobile app testing/performance platform once valued at about $1B. His LinkedIn profile (UC Berkeley High Honors; patents on network testing, data transfer and proxy access devices) shows him now at UR Foundation, building URnetwork, a people-powered encrypted privacy network that he says he started out of a WeWork in Palo Alto.
interesting_fact: URnetwork, which he works on, routes encrypted traffic through community-run nodes and reports 100,000+ providers in 117 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Won a 2011 Eyebeam/Google Data Visualization Challenge award, and his UC Berkeley honors thesis on visualizing movement in multiscale data placed second for best paper.

name: Edward Shenderovich
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Roebling (formerly Synonym), New York - AI engineering for industrial infrastructure
profile: Leningrad-born, UC Berkeley-educated entrepreneur and investor who moved to the US at 14. Was a founding executive of SUP (LiveJournal in Russia), founded Kite Ventures (Delivery Hero, Tradeshift, Plated) and co-founded flex-office company Knotel as executive chairman. Now runs a16z-backed Roebling, an AI-native capital-project planning platform for process engineers in biomanufacturing, chemicals and critical minerals.
interesting_fact: His current company Roebling uses AI to cost and engineer industrial plants 'from R&D to FID' - a direct fit for an energy/infrastructure podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published Russian-language poet: his children's poetry collections came out from Samokat in 2010 and 2014, and 'About One, Two, 3, 4 and 5' won an award at the Biennial of Illustration Bratislava in 2015. In 2000 he also taught business modeling at Università Cattolica in Piacenza, Italy.

public_contacts.value: contact@synonym.bio (legacy Synonym address; company now Roebling)

notes: Knotel (the Hurun-listed unicorn) was sold to Newmark in 2021; avoid dwelling on it. Strong energy/industrial-infrastructure angle via Roebling.

name: Josh Tetrick
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Eat Just, Inc. (consumer brand now 'Just Food Company'; maker of JUST Egg)
profile: Birmingham, Alabama-born former WVU football player with a Cornell BA (Africana studies) and Michigan law degree, who worked in Sub-Saharan Africa on education, UN and investment-law projects. Co-founded Hampton Creek with Josh Balk in 2011 (later Eat Just), building plant-based JUST Egg and cultivated-meat unit GOOD Meat, backed by investors including Li Ka-shing, Peter Thiel and Vinod Khosla.
interesting_fact: Started the company in 2011 with $37,000 of his own money, was featured in Bill Gates' 2013 documentary 'The Future of Food', and is credited with attracting investors including Li Ka-shing, Peter Thiel and Vinod Khosla.
deep_cut_fact: As a West Virginia University football player he shared the team's scout team player of the year award in 2000; before Hampton Creek he briefly worked at TOMS Shoes and launched 33needs, a crowdfunding site for social startups, in January 2011.
notes: Very media-friendly founder and frequent podcast guest. Current 2026 title not independently re-verified (web-search budget exhausted); company site now brands itself Just Food Company.
